_about.what: Neck & back — one move per object in "moves". The app reads this file directly: save it, reload the page. Every field name is checked, so a typo is reported with the file and move it is in.
_about.add: Copy a move that looks like the new one, paste it into "moves", give it a new id and change every field. Or: node scripts/catalog.js new <file> <id>  — writes a template with placeholder text to replace.
_about.remove: Delete the move's object (and the comma before or after it). Routines built in the app that used it will show it as missing.
_about.check: node scripts/catalog.js check  — or reload the app: a bad file shows the error on screen instead of the exercise list.
_about.names: Anything written as a word instead of an object — "metric": "knee", "template": "lean", "preset": "standing", "conditions": "balance" — is looked up in shared.json. Add reusable pieces there, not here.
_about.notes: Any field starting with "_" is a note for people and is ignored: "_note": "physio wants this re-checked".

fields.id: Unique name, used in links and saved sessions — never change it once the move has been used. Lower-case letters, digits, underscores. Good: "seated_knee_ext". Bad: "Seated Knee Ext", "knee-ext", "1_knee".
fields.name: What the user sees in the list. Good: "Seated knee extension". Bad: a clinical term nobody outside physio uses ("Open-chain terminal extension").
fields.clinicalName: Optional. The term a physio would use, shown in the details panel under the name.
fields.type: "reps" (counted) or "hold" (seconds in position). A stretch held for 30 s is a hold; ten slow raises are reps.
fields.view: "side" or "front" — where the phone stands. Side-on for anything that bends forward/back (knees, hips, spine); front-on for anything that goes out to the side (leg raise to the side, arm raise to the side, knees caving in).
fields.tracking: What the camera can honestly do: "form" (counts AND judges — needs at least one fault with a measurement and a threshold), "reps" (counts only; faults are listed for the person to watch), "none" (nothing to measure — the guide is shown and the set is logged by hand). Bad: "form" on a move whose faults are all words; the file will not load.
fields.vetted: Optional, true/false. true = a physio has recorded and checked this move in the Studio; vetted moves list first.
fields.equipment: List of words: ["none"], ["chair"], ["band", "door anchor"]. Optional extras say so: "ankle weight (optional)".
fields.muscles: { "primary": [...], "secondary": [...] } — plain names ("quadriceps", "gluteus medius"). primary must have at least one.
fields.sided: Only for one-sided moves: { "limb": "leg" | "arm" | "side", "by": "camera" | "pick", "auto": true }. "camera" = the limb nearest the phone is the working one (side-on moves); "pick" = the person chooses (front-on moves); "auto": true = when no side was chosen, watch both and follow the one that moves. Leave the field out for two-sided moves.
fields.upperBody: true when the legs need not be in frame (seated desk moves, shoulder work). Default false.
fields.summary: One line for the list. Good: "Sitting, straighten one knee until the leg is level, hold, and lower." Bad: a paragraph.
fields.setup: Where the phone goes and how to start, in the user's words. Good: "Sit tall on a chair, side-on to the phone, working leg nearest…" Bad: "Standard set-up."
fields.why: Why this camera angle can measure this move. Shown to the user; keeps the author honest. Good: "Side-on the knee angle runs from 90° to straight." Bad: left empty.
fields.calibrationPose: Optional. The still position held for the first two seconds of every set, which the coach measures against. Good: "Sitting tall, knee bent to 90°, foot hanging."
fields.camera: { "height": "floor" | "knee" | "hip" | "chest" | "eye", "distance": "2 m", "posture": "standing" | "sitting" | "lying" | "prone" | "sidelying" | "kneeling" }. Leave it out to use the file's default at the top. posture also decides how the stick figure is pinned in place.
fields.targets: Optional list of rep counts / hold seconds the bubble cycles through, e.g. [6, 8, 10, 12]. Leave it out for the standard choices in settings.json.
fields.defaultTarget: The one of targets selected to begin with. Must be in the list. Leave it out with targets.
fields.progress: How far through a rep the person is. { "metric": <measurement>, "start": "calibrated" | number, "target": number | "opt:rom" }. "calibrated" = whatever the measurement reads in the start position; "startMin"/"startMax" clamp it (a knee that calibrates at 150° is treated as 160°). target = the reading at a full rep, or with "targetIsDelta": true a change from the start — "delta": -1 when the reading goes DOWN during the rep (a knee angle closing). Only for type "reps" with tracking "form" or "reps". Good: knee angle from calibrated to 172. Bad: start and target the same number.
fields.hold: For type "hold" with tracking on: { "conditions": [ { "metric": <measurement>, "rel": "abs" | "change", "min": n, "max": n } ] } — the hold counts while every condition is met. "change" = relative to the calibrated start. A condition may carry "when": [{ "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }] so it only applies for that option. A named set ("balance") comes from shared.json.
fields.display: Optional. What the live readout shows: { "label": "bend", "unit": "°", "from": "start" } shows the progress measurement as a change from the start ("abs" = the raw reading); for a hold, { "condition": 0, "label": "knee", "aim": "90°" } shows that hold condition. Without it the app shows the raw progress reading.
fields.enterCue: Optional, holds only: what the coach says when the person has been out of position for a few seconds. Good: "Slide down the wall until your knees are at ninety".
fields.faults: What goes wrong, in the order they matter. Each: { "id", "label", "cue" (spoken, ≤ 8 words, what TO do), "tip" (written, why it matters), "severity" 1–3 }. Add "metric", "op" ("<" or ">"), "threshold" and the camera watches for it; leave those out and it is listed for the person to watch. "minP" (0–1) = ignore until this far into the rep; "persist" ms before it is spoken; "rel": "change" compares to the calibrated start. "when": a list of gates that must all hold for the fault to count — { "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }, { "metric": <measurement>, "op": "<", "threshold": 168 }, "inPosition" or "notInPosition". "phase": "moving" / "rest" (reps) or "any" (a hold fault that must fire while the person is OUT of position; otherwise hold faults only watch the held position). "scale": { "metric": "progress", "times": 0.35 } makes the threshold grow with another reading. Rules instead of a measurement: "rule": "shallow" (rep did not reach the target), "fast" with "minMs", "return" with "threshold" (rep ended above this progress — did not come all the way back). Or "template": "lean" with a "threshold" to reuse one from shared.json. Good cue: "Sit tall". Bad cue: "You are leaning back again" (tells them what is wrong, not what to do).
fields.guide: { "surface": what to stand/lie on, "stop": when to stop, "cannotSee": what the person must check themselves, "regions": [ { "name": "Trunk", "points": [ { "t": "one form point", "tracked": true|false } ] } ] }. tracked: true only when a fault with a measurement actually checks that point — it is shown to the user as "camera watches".
fields.pose: The two-frame stick figure. { "A": start keyframe, "B": end keyframe, "work": { "thigh": 1, "glute": 0.5 } muscles to light up 0–1, "props": [ { "kind": "box" | "bar" | "disc" | "band", "at": "hip" } ], "wall": "behind" | "ahead", "anchor": joint(s) that stay put }. Side-view keyframe angles in degrees: torso (from vertical, + = leaning forward), thigh & shin (from hanging straight down, + = forward), foot (+ = toes up), uarm & farm (arms, + = forward), plus the far limb: thighF, shinF, footF, uarmF, farmF; face: "right" | "left". Front-view: legL, legR, shinL, shinR, armL, armR, foreL, foreR (+ = out to the side), lean, headTilt, squat 0–1. "preset": "standing" | "seated" | "supine" | "prone" | "quadruped" fills the usual values first. Check it on /figures.html.
fields.tempo: Free text. Good: "Up 2 s, hold 2 s, down 3 s."
fields.contraindications: When not to do it. Shown as "Do not do this if".
fields.sources: Optional list of { "name", "url" } added to the file's own sources.
fields.band: Optional. "none", "yellow", "red"… = offers the band-colour bubble with that default; true = offers it defaulting to none.
fields.minMs: Optional, reps only: the quickest a rep may take before "Too fast" fires (when the move lists no live fault of its own). Default in settings.json.
fields.options: Advanced: extra bubbles, e.g. a range target { "key": "rom", "label": "Range target", "values": [45, 60, 75, 90], "unit": "°", "default": 90 } referenced from progress.target as "opt:rom".
fields.figure: Advanced: point keyframes captured by the Studio instead of pose angles. Prefer pose.
fields.focus: Advanced: the landmark the live view highlights, e.g. "KNEE". Default: the last point of the progress measurement.
fields.group: Optional. The heading the move is listed under; default = the file's group at the top.
fields.region: Optional. The body region for filtering; default = the file's region.
fields.icon: Optional short label used where an icon is expected. Default "move".
fields.order: Optional. Position in the list; default = the file's order + position in this file.

moves.name: Upper trapezius stretch
moves.summary: Ear toward the opposite shoulder with the stretched-side hand behind your back — checked for the shoulder creeping up, the head turning and the hand coming out.
moves.setup: Sit or stand facing the camera about 1.5 m away, camera at chest height, head to hips in frame. Put the hand of the side you are stretching behind your back (or sit on it). Tuck the chin slightly, then tilt the ear toward the opposite shoulder; the other hand may rest on the head to add gentle weight. Hold, breathe, keep the stretched shoulder down.
moves.why: From the front the tilt of the head against the line of the shoulders, a shoulder rising toward the ear, and the nose turning away from the camera are all measured directly.

guide.surface: Sitting on a firm chair or standing tall, facing the camera. Camera at chest height, about 1.5 m away, so the head and both shoulders are large in the picture.

points.t: Sit or stand tall, ribs over hips, weight even. Do not slump — the stretch changes completely if the upper back rounds.
Tuck the chin slightly first (retract the head as if making a double chin), then keep that tuck while you tilt.

regions.name: Stretched side (the shoulder that stays down)

points.t: Put that hand behind your back, or sit on it, or hold the chair seat. This anchors the shoulder blade so the stretch goes into the upper trapezius rather than the shoulder joint. The coach checks that the hand is low.
The shoulder must stay down for the whole hold. The moment it creeps up toward the ear the stretch is lost — this is the fault the coach watches most.
Tilt the ear toward the OPPOSITE shoulder (right ear to right shoulder stretches the left trapezius). About 20–30° of tilt is enough; the coach counts the hold once the head is tilted.
Nose and eyes stay pointing at the camera — tilt, do not turn. Turning the head moves the stretch to different muscles and can pinch.
For a stronger stretch, aim the nose slightly toward the armpit (a little forward bend); never push into pain.
The opposite hand may rest lightly on the head to add gentle weight. It rests; it does not pull. If in doubt, leave it in your lap.
Breathe slowly; on each breath out let the shoulder sink a little further from the ear. Mild pull along the side of the neck, never pain or tingling.
Hold 15–30 s, 2–3 times per side. Stretching eases the tightness for a while; pairing it with rows and pull-aparts is what makes it last.

guide.stop: Dizziness, pins and needles into the arm or hand, sharp pain, or a headache that starts during the stretch.

moves.enterCue: Ear toward the shoulder — and keep the other shoulder down
moves.tempo: Ease in over 3 s, hold, breathe.
moves.dosage: 3 × 20–30 s each side, once or twice a day.
moves.progression: Gentle hand weight on the head.
moves.regression: Shorter holds; no hand on the head.
moves.contraindications: Pins and needles down the arm, dizziness, or sharp neck pain.

faults.label: Stretched shoulder creeping up
faults.tip: The stretch only reaches the upper trapezius when the shoulder on the stretched side stays down. Press the hand behind your back toward the floor, or sit on it.

faults.label: Turning the head
faults.tip: Keep the eyes and nose pointing at the camera; turning the head changes which muscle is stretched and can pinch the neck.

faults.label: Hand not behind the back
faults.cue: Put the hand behind your back
faults.tip: The arm behind the back anchors the shoulder blade so the stretch goes into the trapezius, not the shoulder joint.

faults.label: Not tilting enough
faults.cue: Ear a little closer to the shoulder
faults.tip: Tilt until you feel a clear pull along the side of the neck — gentle, never painful. About 20–30° is usually enough.

moves.name: Chin tuck
moves.summary: Glide the chin straight back to make a double chin, hold, release.
moves.setup: Sit or stand tall, side-on to the phone at eye height. Without tipping the head, draw the chin straight back so the ears move over the shoulders. Hold two seconds, release.
moves.why: Side-on, the nose moves closer to the shoulder line with every tuck, so each rep is counted. Whether the head tipped instead of gliding is too subtle to judge.
moves.tempo: Tuck 1 s, hold 2 s, release 1 s.
moves.progression: Hold 5 s; do it lying with the head just off a pillow.
moves.regression: Smaller glide; sit with the back supported.
moves.contraindications: Dizziness, or pain shooting into the arm.

faults.label: Nodding instead of gliding
faults.tip: The chin moves straight back like a drawer closing. If the eyes drop, you are nodding.

faults.label: Shoulders rising
faults.tip: Let the shoulders hang. The neck moves, nothing else.

guide.surface: A chair with a back, or standing against a wall.
guide.stop: Dizziness, or pain or tingling down the arm.
guide.cannotSee: Nodding versus gliding — the difference is a centimetre.

points.t: Ears glide back over the shoulders; eyes stay level.
Relaxed and down.

moves.name: Shoulder blade squeeze
moves.summary: Draw the shoulder blades together and down, as if pinching a pencil between them.
moves.setup: Sit or stand tall. Squeeze the shoulder blades toward each other and slightly down, hold five seconds, relax.
moves.why: The blades move on the back, out of sight of a phone in front. A back-on view sees only a small change. Logged by hand.
moves.progression: Add a light band held in front; progress to rows.
moves.contraindications: Sharp pain between the shoulder blades.

faults.label: Shrugging up
faults.tip: The blades go together and down. If the shoulders rise toward the ears, the upper trapezius has taken over.

faults.label: Arching the lower back
faults.tip: The squeeze happens between the blades, not by throwing the chest forward.

points.t: Blades together and down; shoulders stay low.
Tall, ribs stacked over the hips.

moves.name: Thoracic extension over a roller
moves.summary: A roller across the upper back; hands behind the head, arch backward over it.
moves.setup: Lie with a foam roller across the upper back, knees bent, hands supporting the head. Let the upper back arch over the roller, then come back up. Move the roller a few centimetres and repeat.
moves.why: The arch is small and the head and arms hide the shoulder line from the side. Logged by hand.
moves.regression: Smaller arch; a rolled towel instead of a roller.
moves.contraindications: Osteoporosis, or pain in the lower back during the arch.

faults.label: Arching the lower back instead
faults.tip: Keep the buttocks on the floor and the stomach lightly braced so the arch stays in the upper back.

faults.label: Pulling on the neck
faults.tip: Cradle the head; the neck should feel no strain.

guide.surface: Firm floor with the roller across the shoulder blades.
guide.stop: Lower back pain, or tingling in the arms.
guide.cannotSee: The arch — the head and arms are in the way.

points.t: Arches over the roller, one segment at a time.
Stays on the floor.

moves.name: Levator scapulae stretch
moves.summary: Turn the head toward one armpit and gently draw it down with the hand until the side of the neck stretches.
moves.setup: Sit facing the phone, one hand holding the chair edge to keep that shoulder down. Turn the head toward the opposite armpit and rest the other hand on the back of the head. Let it draw the head gently down. Hold.
moves.why: Facing the phone, the gap between ear and shoulder on the stretched side opens as the head goes down, so the timer only runs while you are actually in the stretch.
moves.tempo: Ease in 5 s, hold, ease out.
moves.progression: Hold the chair to anchor the shoulder more firmly.
moves.regression: No hand on the head; turn and look down only.
moves.contraindications: Dizziness, or pain or tingling into the arm.

faults.label: Stretched-side shoulder rising
faults.tip: Hold the seat of the chair so the shoulder stays anchored; the stretch comes from the head, not the shoulder.

faults.label: Pulling hard with the hand
faults.tip: The hand is a weight resting on the head. Pulling makes the muscle guard.

guide.surface: A chair with an edge to hold.
guide.cannotSee: How hard the hand is pulling.

points.t: Turned toward the armpit and drawn gently down.
Anchored down on the stretched side.

moves.name: Cat–cow
moves.summary: On hands and knees, round the whole back up toward the ceiling, then let it sag and look up.
moves.setup: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, side-on to the phone at knee height. Breathe out and round the back, tucking the chin; breathe in and let the belly drop, lifting the head. Move slowly.
moves.why: From the side the head rises and falls against the shoulder line each cycle, which is enough to count. Whether the whole spine moved or just the neck is not measured.
moves.regression: Seated cat–cow with hands on the knees.
moves.contraindications: Wrist pain that stops weight-bearing; pain on either end of the movement.

faults.label: Only the neck moving
faults.tip: Start each direction at the tailbone and let it travel up; the head is last, not first.

faults.label: Rushing
faults.tip: The movement follows the breath; it should take at least two seconds each direction.

guide.stop: Pain at either end of the range.
guide.cannotSee: Whether the lower back is moving or only the neck.

points.t: Rounds fully, then sags fully — tailbone to head.
Head follows the spine.
Straight, hands under the shoulders.

moves.name: Prone press-up (McKenzie)
moves.summary: Face down, hands under the shoulders, press the upper body up while the hips stay on the floor.
moves.setup: Lie on your front, side-on to the phone at floor level, hands under the shoulders. Press the arms straight to lift the chest, letting the back sag and the hips stay down. Lower slowly.
moves.why: From the side the shoulder–hip line tilts up from the floor each press, so reps are counted. The hips lifting — the one fault that matters — is behind the arms from most angles.
moves.tempo: Up 2 s, hold 2 s, down 2 s.
moves.dosage: 10 reps, every 2 hours in a flare.
moves.progression: Lock the elbows fully; hold the top longer.
moves.contraindications: Pain moving further down the leg on the press — stop and tell your physio.

faults.label: Hips lifting off the floor
faults.tip: Let the pelvis hang heavy; if the hips lift, the arms are doing a push-up instead of an extension.

faults.label: Tensing the back muscles
faults.tip: The arms lift you; the back muscles stay soft so the joints can move.

guide.stop: Pain spreading further down the leg.
guide.cannotSee: The hips lifting, and whether the back is relaxed.

points.t: Arms straighten; chest lifts.
Stays on the floor.

moves.name: Pelvic tilt
moves.summary: Lying with knees bent, flatten the lower back into the floor by tilting the pelvis, then release.
moves.setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Tighten the stomach and press the lower back down so the pelvis rocks back. Hold, then let the natural curve return.
moves.why: The pelvis rocks a few degrees under clothing — invisible to a phone. Logged by hand.
moves.progression: Progress to a dead bug or bridge.
moves.regression: Fewer reps; a pillow under the head.
moves.contraindications: None in most cases — this is usually the first back exercise.

faults.label: Squeezing the buttocks instead
faults.tip: The tilt comes from the abdominals pulling the pelvis; the buttocks stay soft.

faults.label: Holding the breath
faults.tip: The exhale helps the stomach draw in.

points.t: Rocks back; the lower back flattens.

moves.name: Standing back extension
moves.summary: Hands on the hips, lean back from the waist as far as is comfortable, then return.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, feet apart, hands in the small of the back. Keep the knees straight and bend backward from the waist, hold a second, come back up.
moves.why: Side-on, the shoulder–hip line leans back from vertical each rep, so reps are counted.
moves.tempo: Back 2 s, hold 1 s, up 2 s.
moves.regression: Hands higher on the back; smaller lean.
moves.contraindications: Pain spreading down the leg on the lean.

faults.label: Knees bending
faults.tip: Bending the knees turns it into a squat; the movement should come from the back.

faults.label: Throwing the head back
faults.tip: The neck stays in line; bend from the waist.

guide.stop: Pain moving further down the leg.
guide.cannotSee: Whether the lean comes from the lower back or from the knees dropping.

points.t: Leans back from the hips; knees straight.

moves.name: Open book
moves.summary: Lying on your side with knees bent, open the top arm across to the other side like a book.
moves.setup: Lie on one side, knees bent to 90°, arms stacked in front. Keeping the knees together, lift the top arm and sweep it across to the floor behind you, turning the head to follow. Return.
moves.why: The rotation happens in the plane facing the phone only from above; from the floor the arm sweeps toward and away. Logged by hand.
moves.tempo: Open 3 s, hold 2 s, close 3 s.
moves.progression: Hold the open position longer; hold a light weight.
moves.regression: Sweep only as far as the knees stay down.
moves.contraindications: Pain in the shoulder on the sweep.

faults.label: Top knee lifting
faults.tip: If the knees separate, the movement is coming from the lower back instead of the mid-back.

faults.label: Leading with the arm
faults.tip: The arm follows the chest; it does not drag it.

guide.surface: A mat; a pillow under the head.
guide.cannotSee: The sweep — it moves toward the phone.

points.t: Stacked and still.
Rotates open; arm and head follow.

moves.name: Neck isometrics
moves.summary: Press the head into your own hand — forward, back, each side — without letting it move.
moves.setup: Sit tall. Place a palm on the forehead and press the head into it, not moving. Hold five seconds. Repeat with the hand on the back of the head, then each side.
moves.why: Nothing moves by design. Logged by hand.
moves.contraindications: Dizziness or headache during the press.

faults.label: Head moving
faults.tip: The hand and head cancel each other out; if the head moves, ease off.

faults.label: Holding the breath
faults.tip: Count out loud through the hold.

points.t: Still, pressing evenly into the hand.

moves.name: Seated thoracic rotation
moves.summary: Arms crossed on the chest, turn the upper body as far as it goes each way, hips still.
moves.setup: Sit tall on a chair facing the phone, knees together, arms crossed. Turn the chest to one side as far as is comfortable, return, then the other side.
moves.why: Turning toward and away from the phone changes the shoulder width on screen, but not reliably enough to count. Logged by hand.
moves.tempo: Turn 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s.
moves.progression: A stick across the shoulders; a slightly further turn.
moves.contraindications: Sharp pain in the mid-back during the turn.

faults.label: Hips turning too
faults.tip: Squeeze the knees together so the turn happens above the waist.

faults.label: Leaning instead of turning
faults.tip: Keep the head level and the trunk tall.

points.t: Turns fully each way.
Face the phone throughout.

moves.name: Child's pose
moves.summary: From kneeling, sit the hips back onto the heels and reach the arms forward along the floor.
moves.setup: Kneel on a mat side-on to the phone at floor level. Sit back toward the heels and walk the hands forward until the forehead is near the floor. Breathe into the back and hold.
moves.why: From the side the knee is fully folded while you sit back, so the timer runs only while the hips are actually down.
moves.tempo: Ease in over a breath; hold.
moves.progression: Walk the hands to one side to stretch the flank.
moves.regression: A cushion between the calves and the hips.
moves.contraindications: Knee pain when folding; pregnancy after the second trimester.

faults.label: Hips coming up
faults.tip: If the hips hover, put a cushion behind the knees so you can rest rather than hold.

faults.label: Shoulders up around the ears
faults.tip: Let the arms be heavy; the reach comes from the hips going back.

points.t: Resting toward the heels.
Long on the floor ahead.

moves.name: Knee to chest
moves.summary: On your back, hug one knee toward the chest and hold.
moves.setup: Lie on your back, side-on to the phone at floor level, working leg nearest. Draw the knee toward the chest with both hands and hold, the other leg straight or bent.
moves.why: From the side the hip angle closes as the knee comes in, so the timer runs while the knee is actually held close.
moves.tempo: Draw in over a breath; hold; release.
moves.regression: Hold behind the thigh instead of over the shin.
moves.contraindications: Hip pinching at the front, or pain down the leg.

faults.label: Head and shoulders lifting
faults.tip: The knee comes to you; you do not go to the knee. Rest the head.

faults.label: Yanking the knee
faults.tip: Draw steadily; the muscle lets go only if the pull is gentle.

guide.stop: Pain down the leg, or pinching in the hip.
guide.cannotSee: How hard the hands are pulling.

points.t: Knee held close to the chest.
Resting on the floor.

moves.name: Lower trunk rotation
moves.summary: Lying with knees bent, let the knees roll gently side to side while the shoulders stay flat.
moves.setup: Lie on your back, knees bent and together, arms out to the sides. Let the knees fall slowly to one side as far as is comfortable, bring them back, then the other side.
moves.why: The knees roll toward and away from a phone on the floor, and a phone overhead is impractical. Logged by hand.
moves.tempo: Over 3 s, hold 2 s, back 3 s.
moves.progression: Feet off the floor with the knees at 90°.
moves.contraindications: Sharp back pain on the roll.

faults.label: Shoulder lifting
faults.tip: Roll only as far as both shoulders stay on the floor.

faults.label: Knees separating
faults.tip: Keep the knees glued so both hips roll as one.

points.t: Together, rolling as one.
Flat on the floor.
